issues.quote: It has run badly for ten years. I have never let anyone regulate it, not a watchmaker, not even Uncle
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives only one reading error: at nine o'clock the watch showed 8:40. It says nothing about the watch running badly over time or drifting.
issues.misreading: 'Run badly for ten years' suggests an irregular or drifting error rather than a fixed 20-minute offset. A solver could conclude the watch's error changed through the night, so none of Monnier's later readings (10:15, 10:18, 10:21, 10:32) can be reliably converted to true time, which would undermine the timeline.

issues.quote: I had brandy, I will admit that, more than I should have.
issues.fact: The fact sheet does not mention drinking. The statement is extra detail that the sheet does not support.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a reason to doubt the accuracy of Monnier's perceptions and times, and discount his readings more than the fact sheet intends.

issues.quote: Four years on one watch, and he meant it to strike the first minute of the new century.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for the repeater's making or any link to the new century.
issues.misreading: It adds a duration hint about the repeater's construction that the sheet does not give, which a solver could use as a clue.
